Here is a detailed 14-day beginner machine learning plan that satisfies all constraints and success criteria. The plan balances theory and practical exercises, covers all required topics, and reserves the final two days for revision and a small project.

### **14-Day Beginner Machine Learning Learning Plan**

#### **Day 1: Introduction to Machine Learning**
- **Theory:**
  - What is machine learning?
  - Types of machine learning (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning)
  - Common applications of ML
- **Practical:**
  - Set up Python environment (Jupyter Notebook, Anaconda, or VS Code)
  - Install necessary libraries (NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Seaborn)
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Introduction](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/getting_started.html)
  - [Kaggle Python for Data Science](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/python)

---

#### **Day 2: Python for Machine Learning**
- **Theory:**
  - Python basics (variables, loops, functions, lists, dictionaries)
  - Working with libraries (NumPy, Pandas)
- **Practical:**
  - Create a simple script to load and explore a dataset (e.g., Iris dataset)
  - Use Pandas to manipulate data (filtering, grouping, basic statistics)
- **Resources:**
  - [Pandas Documentation](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/)
  - [NumPy Tutorial](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/quickstart.html)

---

#### **Day 3: Data Preprocessing**
- **Theory:**
  - Importance of data preprocessing
  - Handling missing values, outliers, and categorical data
  - Feature scaling and normalization
- **Practical:**
  - Load a dataset (e.g., Titanic dataset)
  - Preprocess data (handle missing values, encode categorical variables, scale features)
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Preprocessing](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/preprocessing.html)
  - [Kaggle Data Preprocessing Tutorial](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/preprocessing)

---

#### **Day 4: Introduction to Supervised Learning**
- **Theory:**
  - What is supervised learning?
  - Types of supervised learning (regression, classification)
  - Overview of common algorithms (Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees)
- **Practical:**
  - Implement a simple linear regression model using Scikit-learn
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Supervised Learning](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/supervised_learning.html)
  - [Kaggle Supervised Learning Guide](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/supervised-learning)

---

#### **Day 5: Linear Regression**
- **Theory:**
  - How linear regression works
  - Cost function and gradient descent
- **Practical:**
  - Train a linear regression model on a dataset (e.g., Boston Housing dataset)
  - Evaluate the model using metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R²
- **Resources:**
  - [Linear Regression in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression.html)
  - [Kaggle Linear Regression Tutorial](https://www.kaggle.com/code/pratik0300/linear-regression-with-python/notebook)

---

#### **Day 6: Classification Basics**
- **Theory:**
  - What is classification?
  - Logistic Regression (binary classification)
  - Confusion matrix and classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score)
- **Practical:**
  - Train a logistic regression model on a binary classification dataset (e.g., Iris dataset for binary classification)
  - Evaluate the model using classification metrics
- **Resources:**
  - [Logistic Regression in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression.html)
  - [Kaggle Classification Guide](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/classification)

---

#### **Day 7: Model Evaluation**
- **Theory:**
  - Cross-validation
  - Train-test split
  - Overfitting and underfitting
- **Practical:**
  - Use cross-validation to evaluate a model
  - Split data into training and testing sets and compare performance
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Model Evaluation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html)
  - [Kaggle Model Evaluation](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/model-evaluation)

---

#### **Day 8: Decision Trees and Random Forest**
- **Theory:**
  - How decision trees work
  - Random Forest algorithm
- **Practical:**
  - Train a decision tree classifier on a dataset (e.g., Iris dataset)
  - Train a Random Forest classifier and compare performance
- **Resources:**
  - [Decision Trees in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/tree.html)
  - [Random Forest in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier.html)

---

#### **Day 9: Introduction to Unsupervised Learning**
- **Theory:**
  - What is unsupervised learning?
  - Clustering (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering)
  - Dimensionality Reduction (PCA)
- **Practical:**
  - Apply K-Means clustering on a dataset (e.g., Iris dataset)
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Unsupervised Learning](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/supervised_learning.html#unsupervised-learning)
  - [K-Means Clustering Tutorial](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_digits.html)

---

#### **Day 10: K-Means Clustering**
- **Theory:**
  - How K-Means works
  - Choosing the optimal number of clusters (Elbow Method)
- **Practical:**
  - Use the Elbow Method to determine the best number of clusters
  - Visualize clusters using Matplotlib/Seaborn
- **Resources:**
  - [K-Means in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.cluster.KMeans.html)
  - [Elbow Method Guide](https://www.kaggle.com/code/pratik0300/k-means-clustering/notebook)

---

#### **Day 11: Dimensionality Reduction (PCA)**
- **Theory:**
  - What is PCA?
  - How PCA reduces dimensionality
- **Practical:**
  - Apply PCA to a dataset and visualize the reduced dimensions
- **Resources:**
  - [PCA in Scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.decomposition.PCA.html)
  - [PCA Tutorial](https://www.kaggle.com/code/pratik0300/pca-in-python/notebook)

---

#### **Day 12: Review and Mini-Project Preparation**
- **Theory:**
  - Recap of all topics covered so far
  - Overview of the mini-project
- **Practical:**
  - Choose a dataset for the mini-project (e.g., Titanic, Iris, or another dataset)
  - Outline the steps for the project (data loading, preprocessing, modeling, evaluation)
- **Resources:**
  - [Kaggle Datasets](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets)

---

#### **Day 13: Mini-Project Work**
- **Practical:**
  - Implement the mini-project:
    - Load and preprocess the dataset
    - Train a supervised or unsupervised model
    - Evaluate the model and visualize results
  - Example project ideas:
    - Predict house prices using regression
    - Classify iris species using classification
    - Cluster customer data using K-Means
- **Resources:**
  - [Kaggle Notebooks](https://www.kaggle.com/notebooks)

---

#### **Day 14: Revision and Final Project Submission**
- **Theory:**
  - Review all key concepts and practical exercises
  - Troubleshoot common issues
- **Practical:**
  - Finalize the mini-project
  - Present the project (explain the approach, results, and insights)
  - Reflect on what was learned and areas for improvement
- **Resources:**
  - [Scikit-learn Cheat Sheet](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/tutorial/basic/tutorial.html)
  - [Kaggle Learning Path](https://www.kaggle.com/learn)

---

This plan ensures that you cover all the required topics, include both theory and practical exercises, and reserve the final two days for revision and a small project.
